# ui::Signal

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

Derives from `ui::PropertyBase`.

An event with no value, meaning "ask again".

The same edge list as a [Property](property.md) and the same two-way lifetime safety, with no value and so no equality gate: [raise()](#raise) always reaches every observer. A copy (or a move) is a different object with no observers of its own. Assigning to a Signal keeps the observers it has, since they observe this object and not the one it was assigned from. A struct holding one therefore stays an ordinary copyable aggregate.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Signal settings_changed;
ui::Subscription reload = settings_changed.observe([&] { std::println("Reloading the settings"); });

// Every save raises it, and every raise() runs the handler again, even when nothing in the
// file changed, since a Signal has no value to compare.
window.set_content(ui::Button{.text = "Save", .on_click = [&] { save(); settings_changed.raise(); }});
```

## Signal

```cpp
Signal() = default
```

A signal with no observers.

## ~Signal

```cpp
~Signal() = default
```

Leaves every remaining [Subscription](subscription.md) dead.

## Signal

```cpp
Signal(const Signal&) noexcept
```

A fresh signal with no observers; `other`'s observers are not copied.

## operator=

```cpp
Signal& operator=(const Signal&) noexcept
```

No-op: this signal keeps its own observers.

## observe

```cpp
Subscription observe(Callback<void()> fn) const
```

Observe. The returned [Subscription](subscription.md) must be kept for `fn` to keep firing.

## raise

```cpp
void raise(std::source_location where = std::source_location::current()) const
```

Tell every observer. Const: raising changes nothing a reader of the signal can see, and the objects that own one are handed around by const pointer (a control's [ui::CommandRef](../tree/command-ref.md)).

## observer_count

```cpp
std::size_t observer_count() const noexcept
```

How many live subscriptions observe this signal.
